saccade.equation: durationMs = interceptMs + slopeMsPerDeg * amplitudeDeg; position follows a minimum-jerk profile 10 s^3 - 15 s^4 + 6 s^5 of normalized time s
saccade.citation: Carpenter RHS, Movements of the Eyes, 2nd ed., Pion, 1988 (D = 21 + 2.2 A, as quoted by Devillez et al. 2020, Visual Cognition; excerpt). The master plan attributed the line to Bahill, Clark & Stark 1975, who introduced the main sequence. The minimum-jerk profile is a modeling choice for the trajectory shape.

vergence.citation: latencyS: 160 ms, attributed to Westheimer & Mitchell 1956 by a later review (excerpt); a model-based study puts it at 80-120 ms. timeConstantS: master plan value for Rashbass & Westheimer, J Physiol 159:339-360, 1961 (doi 10.1113/jphysiol.1961.sp006812), not confirmed against the paper.

accommodation.citation: Master plan values for Kasthurirangan & Glasser, Age related changes in accommodative dynamics in humans, Vision Res 46:1507-1519, 2006 (doi 10.1016/j.visres.2005.11.012), not confirmed against the paper's tables. Excerpts confirm that accommodation latency does not change with age (14-45 y) while the accommodation time constant increases; blur-driven latency is about 300 ms (review excerpt). Age dependence is not modeled.
